chunks: And with this chain of narrators, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Verily, Allah the Great and Almighty has a pillar of red ruby, the top of which is under the Throne, and the bottom of which is on the back of the fish in the lowest seventh Earth. When a servant says: 'There is no god but Allah', the Throne trembles, and the pillar moves, and the fish moves. So Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: 'Remain calm, O My Throne!' It replies: 'How shall I remain calm when You have not forgiven the one who uttered it?' Then Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: 'Bear witness, O inhabitants of My heavens, that indeed I have forgiven the one who uttered it.'

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the cosmological effect of reciting 'La ilaha illa Allah' according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this cosmological narrative to illustrate the metaphysical weight of Tawhid, where the physical trembling of the Throne and the ruby pillar signifies the immediate impact of divine declaration on the universe. The dialogue between the Throne and God highlights a unique Shia theological nuance: the Throne’s reluctance to rest until forgiveness is confirmed, emphasizing that the utterance of monotheism is not merely verbal but a catalyst for divine mercy. This imagery reinforces the concept that the believer's declaration actively participates in the cosmic order, bridging the earthly realm with the divine presence.
